sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 3.3% a year, from $65.1 billion in FY2017 to $87.0 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F201].
Operating margin fell to 8.1% in FY2019 [F23], the window low [D646], from 21.2% in FY2017 [F21].

The FY2019 drop reflects an $8.3 billion asset impairment [X112], including a $6.8 billion Shave Care goodwill write-down [X109], which the filing attributes to currency devaluations and slowing grooming category growth [P62].
Margin recovered to 22.1% in FY2020 [F24] as operating income rose $10.2 billion, of which $8.3 billion was the base-period impairment [P71].
Non-US sales, 52.0% of revenue [D509], added 3.1pp of FY2026's 3.3% growth [D511][D457], against 0.1pp from the US [D536].
The filing attributes the year's net sales growth to favourable foreign exchange and pricing, with unit volume and mix unchanged [P26].
Beauty was the largest segment contributor at 1.3pp on 7.1% growth [D603][D602], ahead of Fabric Home Care at 0.8pp [D543].
Operating income fell 3.4% [D458] on 3.3% revenue growth [D457], an incremental margin of -25.6% [D481].
Diluted EPS rose 1.7% [D461] against 0.5% net income growth [D459] because the diluted share count fell 1.3% [D476].
Operating margin was 22.7% in FY2026 [F30], below the FY2025 high of 24.3% [D647] and above the 22.1% window median [D648].
Cost of revenue took 1.0pp off the margin [D483] and SG&A 0.6pp [D485], with the filing citing lower gross margin and higher marketing spending [P25].
Net margin fell 0.5pp to 18.4% [D471][F50] as the effective tax rate rose to 20.8% [D443] on lower share-based compensation benefits [P23].
Other income of $1.1 billion [X108] included the Glad joint venture gain [P24], which flatters FY2026 net margin relative to operating margin.
Operating cash flow of $19.6 billion [F80] was 1.22x net income [D444], and free cash flow of $15.1 billion [F100] was 0.94x [D445], below the 1.02x window median [D660].
Working capital was a partial offset: inventory build used $641 million [P3], against $919 million generated by payables [P3].
Capex rose to $4.41 billion [F90], 1.40x D&A [D446] from 1.33x in FY2025 [D395]; the filing cites capex only as the main driver of investing outflows and gives no reason for the rise [P2].
Net cash improved slightly to -$24.2 billion [D450] from -$24.9 billion [D399], or -27.8% of revenue [D451].
That places P&G at the 33rd percentile of six staples peers, against a peer median of -1.0% [D676][D677].
The current ratio was 0.68x [F180] against a window median of 0.72x [D663], and has been below 1.0x in every year of the window [F171][F180].
Buybacks of $5.03 billion [X134] and dividends of $10.2 billion [X144] totalled $15.3 billion [D452], 100.7% of free cash flow [D453], while diluted shares fell 1.3% [D476].
The current ratio below 1.0x [R1] is 0.68x in FY2026 [F180] and under 1.0x every year since FY2017 [F171], so it looks structural; the passages cited do not explain it.
Buybacks and dividends exceeded free cash flow in FY2025 (116.6%) [D402] and FY2026 (100.7%) [D453] [R2]; total debt grew 6.3% [D427] in FY2025, which suggests borrowing helped fund the gap.
Operating income fell 3.4% in FY2026 [D458] and operating margin 1.6pp [D470], the filing citing lower gross margin and higher marketing spend [P25].
Data quality: FY2018 passages quote net earnings of $2.3 billion [P75], far from the reported $9.75 billion [F32], so I do not use them to explain FY2018.
Operating margin holding at or above the 22.1% window median [D648], from 22.7% in FY2026 [F30], would confirm the margin base; a fall below it would reverse the trend in the FY2027 10-K.
Free cash flow margin staying above the 17.2% window median [D654], against 17.4% in FY2026 [D441], would show cash generation keeping pace with payouts in the FY2027 10-K.
US sales growth, 0.2% in FY2026 [D535], returning above the FY2025 rate of 2.7% [D532] would confirm a US recovery in the FY2027 10-K.
